lines.text: This is Dhaka.
And you've made up your mind. Japan is next.
Maybe it's work.
Maybe it's a degree.
Or a trip you've been saving up for.
Getting there is the easy part.
Almost five thousand kilometers. A few hours in the air.
Then you land.
And everything around you is in Japanese.
次は、新宿です。
The announcement on the train.
The form at the city office.
The first question in your job interview.
自己紹介をお願いします。
A ticket gets you to Japan.
The language is what lets you live there.
Japanese Shikhi teaches Japanese in Bangla, from your first hiragana to JLPT N1.
Every grammar point is explained in Bangla.
New words come back for review just before you'd forget them.
And when you're ready, there's listening practice and timed mock exams.
Going for work? Japan's skilled worker visa asks for N4, or an equivalent test.
Going to study? Many universities that teach in Japanese expect N2.
Travelling? Even the basics make each day easier.
Wherever you're headed, start here. In Bangla.
日本で会いましょう。
